problem: For a Poisson-binomial pmf with variance V >= 1 and first-descent index D, prove a variance-scaled lower bound V(1 - f_{D-1} f_{D+1}/f_D^2) >= 1/4 on the normalized Turán (log-concavity) slack at D, with the constant shown to be at best 1/3.
debate: The literature on quantitative strengthenings of log-concavity (Newton/Turán-type inequalities) for Bernoulli sums, namely the Hillion–Johnson and Johnson lower bounds on the Turán deficit, plus Darroch's mode theorem and the Bobkov–Marsiglietti–Melbourne maximal-mass bounds; the opening calls it a literature, not a debate.
gap: Existing lower bounds on the Turán deficit scale with n or with the success probabilities and degenerate when many summands with p_i near 0 or 1 accumulate at fixed variance, while mode and maximal-mass results do not control the deficit at all.
contribution: A variance-only lower bound V*delta_D >= 1/4 (hence f_{D+r}/f_D <= exp(-r/(4V))), a binomial family showing no constant above 1/3 works, and a computer-assisted proof combining cubic inequalities, a maximal-mass bound and exact Bernstein expansions.
note: The claim, gap and result are legible, but you never say why the Turán deficit at the first descent matters beyond a one-line tail bound and a passing mention of Stirling/Eulerian rows, and the open gap between 1/4 and 1/3 plus a computer-assisted proof of a single-index inequality makes ECP significance the thing referees will probe.
